runs.name: Matrix Service Company; Nasdaq MTRX, SEC CIK 0000866273, fiscal year to June 30; engineering, fabrication, construction and maintenance for energy and industrial infrastructure in Storage and Terminal Solutions, Utility and Power Infrastructure and Process and Industrial Facilities; the ABL with Bank of Montreal extended to 2029 on 2025-08-22
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$10.02** a share (close 2026-10-16, `tools/run.py` quote source, aggregator, flagged). Shares **28,291,921**, one class (10-K FY2026, `0000866273-26-000057`, cover as of 2026-09-02; `Screens/cover_shares.py` the same; checked against 28,133,850 issued and outstanding at 2026-06-30 with no treasury shares, the rise restricted-stock vesting; no later 8-K issuing shares); cap **$283.5M**. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury 30-year par yield, 2026-10-16). Documents read: 10-K FY2026 (`0000866273-26-000057`), DEF 14A of 2026-09-23 (`0001140361-26-037426`), the 8-K of 2026-09-02 and its earnings release (`0000866273-26-000053`), the 8-K of 2025-08-25 (ABL amendment, maturity 2029, `0000866273-25-000037`), the 8-K of 2022-09-30 (Nasdaq late-filing notice, `0000866273-22-000097`), the 10-Ks FY2023 (`0000866273-23-000058`), FY2022 (`0000866273-22-000105`) and FY2021 (`0000866273-21-000088`); FY2010 to FY2020 from XBRL company facts, transcription, flagged. Cross-check: FY2026 revenue $873,632 thousand on the filed income statement against 873.6 tagged; operating cash $6,907 thousand and capital spending $5,483 thousand against `tools/run.py`'s 6.9 and 5.5. The brief's two stated departures: lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 (listed in the run file); the 10-K names no rival, so Primoris (PRIM), MYR Group (MYRG) and Argan (AGX) read as a CONVENTION of the run, no SEC filer found whose main business is specialty storage tanks; rival figures XBRL transcriptions, flagged. **Q1 IN**, narrowly **[M2012-065]**, **[M2011-014]**, **[M1998-044]**: a mid-sized bidder for fixed-price industrial construction ($682.9M of $873.6M of FY2026 revenue fixed-price), economics foreseeable in kind from sixteen years of filings, the doubt about amount and timing carried to Q2 and Q7. **Q2 OUT** **[M2011-015]**, **[M2005-020]**, **[M1997-010]**, **[L2007-004]**: "We competitively bid most of our projects" and "Competitive pressures may require us to accept lower margins, assume greater contractual risk" on the filer's own words, a client moving an award away over risk terms in FY2026; gross margin below Primoris's in every year 2011 to 2025 and below MYR Group's in every year but 2011, operating margin negative every year FY2020 to FY2026; cumulative operating income FY2010 to FY2026 about -$48M on about $16B of revenue; the parts rule applied both ways (the five-year total negative, the CONVENTION's "largest part" not saying largest by what): Storage and Terminal, largest by revenue, an operating loss in four of five years on gross margins 0.1% to 6.1%; Utility and Power, largest by operating income, one good year in five, gross margin below MYR's each year, one customer 53.3% of its FY2026 revenue, backlog $346.4M to $145.7M; the field's returns ordinary (Primoris 2.9% to 6.8%, MYR 1.6% to 6.2% operating); the change for the better (FY2026 gross margin 7.3%, operating margin -1.1%) considered and not credited, since credited in full it would still sit below the ordinary field; OUT and not TOO HARD (NATURE). Q3 to Q12 not reached. Facts after the stop, recorded not judged: integrity facts (the FY2022 10-K filed late, project time booked to overhead, found immaterial by an outside review; the FY2026 annual incentive paid on adjusted operating income plus net interest income in a year of a $9.6M GAAP operating loss; the earnings release headlining Adjusted EBITDA $16.0M, excluding stock pay and restructuring, against a GAAP net loss of $2.6M; restructuring charged six years running; the CEO, CFO and chief administrative officer gone in 2026, the former CEO paid $6,741,465 including $1.6M severance; a director not independent, his son the General Counsel); retained earnings $239.5M (2019) to $1.9M (2026), goodwill and intangibles $139.8M (2017) to $28.9M after impairments; cash $43.8M to $223.0M as billings in excess of costs rose $75.1M to $299.9M; no borrowings, ABL $90M, $237.2M of surety bonds, multiemployer pensions with withdrawal liability undetermined; buyback prices not read. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash (operating cash less stock pay less capital spending) $57.8M / $100.9M / -$5.7M (FY2024 to FY2026), literal window FY2022 to FY2026 mean $16.4M; FY2022 aberrational, cycle base FY2019 to FY2025 at $15.44M before interest; growth traced to the customer-advance build cut by (f) to the business's own sales growth, -7.93% a year, carried by (b) as the bottom; value range $13.26 to $17.93 a share all-equity against $10.02 (equity-only $5.37 to $10.04); fair $12.23 all-equity, $4.35 equity-only; the analyst's flag: the central figure counts customers' prepayments twice ($204.5M of the cycle's owner cash was the rise in billings in excess of costs, and the $223.0M of cash is added again as net cash); before the advance build, about -$10.65 a share; not armed (box OUT at Q2). Contamination declared by the analyst: the LGN commit subjects, AYI and ARCB folder names in the git status, a memory index line, and one file-name filter of the `Test Runs/` listing for MTRX or Matrix before the blind rule was applied with care, returning nothing (the self-audit box left unticked for it); none used. Commits 8d5c9ad9 (template), c315ca83 (Step 0, Q1), 306c7fe0 (Q2), 2118ccb3 (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` PASS (29 ids, 19 fragments); the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py`, 14 quoted fragments beside an id, all in their rows: **no slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q2's parts CONVENTION, "the largest part", does not say largest by what when the whole loses money; (2) the change-for-the-better CONVENTION does not say what follows when the improvement, credited in full, would still show no castle; (3) Q7 counts a contractor's customer advances twice, in owner cash under (d) and again as net cash, with no mirror of the floor-plan CONVENTION; (4) (a) does not choose between peak-to-peak and trough-to-trough cycles (FY2019 to FY2025 at $15.4M against FY2018 to FY2022 at about $2.2M); (5) the self-audit has no line for a file-name search made before the blind rule was applied. Could not get: an SEC filer whose main business is specialty storage tanks, the prices paid for past buybacks, filed statements for FY2010 to FY2020, any scuttlebutt.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 (Matrix Service Company, Nasdaq MTRX; engineering, fabrication, construction and maintenance for energy and industrial infrastructure in Storage and Terminal Solutions, Utility and Power Infrastructure and Process and Industrial Facilities). Q1 IN narrowly; Q2 OUT: a fixed-price bidder on its own words, gross margin below Primoris's every year 2011 to 2025 and below MYR Group's every year but 2011, operating losses every year FY2020 to FY2026, cumulative operating income about -$48M on about $16B of revenue since FY2010; neither deciding part shows a castle; the FY2026 improvement, credited in full, still below the ordinary field. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the late FY2022 10-K, a bonus on an adjusted figure in a GAAP loss year, Adjusted EBITDA featured, the top three officers gone in 2026. Computation beneath the stop $13.26 to $17.93 all-equity against $10.02, fair $12.23 all-equity ($4.35 equity-only), resting on customer advances counted twice, about -$10.65 a share before them; not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: the parts rule when the whole loses money, a change for the better that cannot show a castle, customer advances counted twice in Q7, which cycle is the last full one, a self-audit line for an early file-name search.
